request.question: Compare the 2025 and 2026 Cedar Bay policies: annual training days in each, the increase in days and percent, and which policy supersedes which. Cite both source documents.

comparison.actual_answer:
Summary
- The 2025 Cedar Bay policy (historical) grants 10 days per year of annual training to all fictional staff. (Source: 01-policy-2025.txt)
- The 2026 Cedar Bay policy (active) grants 15 days per year of annual training. (Source: 02-policy-2026-table.pdf)
- The 2026 policy is explicitly identified as active and supersedes the 2025 training policy. (Source: 02-policy-2026-table.pdf)

Details from each document
- 2025 policy (01-policy-2025.txt)
  - Document identification: SYNTHETIC / FICTIONAL / UNCLASSIFIED EVALUATION; Person: Maya Chen; Place: Cedar Bay; Document type: Policy; Version: 2025; historical. (Source: 01-policy-2025.txt)
  - Annual training allowance: 10 days. The file states: "Annual training allowance: 10 days." and notes it "Applies to all fictional staff." (Source: 01-policy-2025.txt)

- 2026 policy (02-policy-2026-table.pdf)
  - Document identification: SYNTHETIC / FICTIONAL / UNCLASSIFIED; Person: Omar Patel; Place: Cedar Bay; Document type: Policy; Version: 2026; active. It is described as superseding the 2025 training policy. (Source: 02-policy-2026-table.pdf)
  - Annual training allowance: 15 days per year. The table in the document shows "Annual training — 15 Days/year." (Source: 02-policy-2026-table.pdf)

Numeric comparison: increase in days and percent
- Raw increase in days:
  - 2026 days − 2025 days = 15 − 10 = 5 additional days per year. (Sources: 02-policy-2026-table.pdf; 01-policy-2025.txt)

- Percent increase calculation:
  - Percent increase = (Increase ÷ Original amount) × 100%
  - Using 2025 as the original amount: (5 ÷ 10) × 100% = 0.5 × 100% = 50%
  - Therefore, the 2026 policy represents a 50% increase in annual training days relative to the 2025 policy. (Sources: 01-policy-2025.txt; 02-policy-2026-table.pdf)

Supersession and status
- The 2026 policy is explicitly marked active and is described as superseding the 2025 training policy. The 2025 policy is described as historical (Version: 2025; historical). Thus:
  - Which policy supersedes which: The 2026 Cedar Bay policy supersedes the 2025 Cedar Bay policy. (Source confirming supersession and active/historical status: 02-policy-2026-table.pdf; 01-policy-2025.txt)

Contextual notes drawn from the documents
- Both documents are labeled synthetic, fictional, and unclassified. The 2025 historical policy names Maya Chen; the 2026 active policy names Omar Patel. The 2025 document specifies its 10-day annual training allowance applies to all fictional staff; the 2026 table lists the allowance as 15 days/year. (Sources: 01-policy-2025.txt; 02-policy-2026-table.pdf)

Concise answer (directly addressing the requested comparison)
- Annual training days: 2025 = 10 days/year (01-policy-2025.txt); 2026 = 15 days/year (02-policy-2026-table.pdf).
- Increase in days: +5 days/year (15 − 10 = 5). (Sources: 02-policy-2026-table.pdf; 01-policy-2025.txt)
- Percent increase: 50% increase ((5 ÷ 10) × 100% = 50%). (Sources: 01-policy-2025.txt; 02-policy-2026-table.pdf)
- Supersession: The 2026 policy (active) supersedes the 2025 policy (historical). (Source: 02-policy-2026-table.pdf; corroborating 01-policy-2025.txt)

Sources cited
- 01-policy-2025.txt — SYNTHETIC / FICTIONAL / UNCLASSIFIED EVALUATION. Person: Maya Chen; Place: Cedar Bay; Document type: Policy; Version: 2025; historical. Annual training allowance: 10 days. Applies to all fictional staff. (Source: 01-policy-2025.txt)
- 02-policy-2026-table.pdf — SYNTHETIC / FICTIONAL / UNCLASSIFIED. Person: Omar Patel; Place: Cedar Bay; Document type: Policy; Version: 2026; active; supersedes the 2025 training policy. Table: Annual training — 15 days/year. (Source: 02-policy-2026-table.pdf)
